verses.text: On another day the angels came to stand before the LORD, and Satan came with them to stand before the LORD too.
The LORD asked Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "From wandering around the earth, going back and forth across it."

Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him. He is a good man with no fault in him. He is honest, he respects God, and he stays away from evil. He is still faithful, even though you talked me into letting you ruin him for no reason."
Satan answered the LORD, "Skin for skin! A man will give up everything he has to save his own life.
But reach out your hand and hurt his body, his bones and flesh, and he will curse you to your face."
The LORD said to Satan, "All right. He is in your power. But you must spare his life."
So Satan left the LORD's presence and struck Job with painful sores from the bottom of his feet to the top of his head.
Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself, and he sat among the ashes.
His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your faithfulness? Curse God and die!"
But Job answered, "You are talking like a foolish woman. Should we accept only good things from God and not trouble?" In all this, Job did not sin in anything he said.

Job had three friends: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah. When they heard about all the trouble that had come to Job, each of them left his home. They agreed to meet together and go to show Job their sympathy and comfort him.
When they saw Job from far away, they could hardly recognize him. They began to cry out loud. They tore their robes and threw dust into the air and onto their heads.
Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.
